designNarrative: LocationsView.vue's onMounted swaps the network-dependent L.tileLayer(OSM) call for a single L.imageOverlay() over a new in-repo SVG, kept inside Leaflet's default EPSG:3857 CRS so the real-geography assertions in map.spec.ts stay valid; the asset and its CC BY 4.0 licence note sit flat in public/ alongside the app's other static assets, and a new Playwright test blocks every off-origin request and directly verifies the image overlay's own load success. Behaviour change: yes — the map's visual tile source moves from live internet tiles to a static local image.
securitySurface: Removes the view's only external network call (tile.openstreetmap.org) — reduces exfiltration/SSRF-adjacent surface; no new trust boundary is introduced by the image overlay, which is served same-origin from public/.
performanceSurface: No per-tile network fetches on pan/zoom — eliminates external request latency and flakiness entirely, which is the point of the change.
Static single-image overlay cannot stream additional detail on zoom the way tiles could, but architecture-notes.md already priced this trade-off as a non-issue for a fixed-purpose test fixture view.
